Zayn al-Din, the Turkish emir who was the governor of Qutb al-Din, the lord of Mosul,
when he grew old, became feeble, and went blind,
surrendered the districts that were under his hand,
namely Sinjar, Harran, the fortress of Aqr, the fortresses of Hakkari, Tikrit, and Shahrazur,
to Qutb al-Din.
And he left nothing for himself except Arbela alone,
because it had belonged to him from the time of the Atabeg Zengi.
And he moved to it,
and he died in it.
And after him arose his son Muzaffar al-Din,
and his governor became Mujahid al-Din.
It is said concerning this Zayn al-Din
that he was a Turkish emir,
and to his justice, his alms, and his generosity there was no end.
And although he was shrewder than anyone,
he would display simplicity.
For one of the horsemen came to him
with the tail of a horse in his hand,
and showed it, saying: "My horse has died."
And he commanded,
and a horse was given to him.
And he took the tail and went,
and gave it to another.
And that one also came and showed that his horse had died.
And he commanded, and gave a horse to him also.
And in this way, hand to hand,
twelve of them brought that same tail,
and to all twelve he gave a horse.
And to that last one he said:
"How is it that you are not ashamed before me,
as I am before you? For behold, fourteen times this very tail has been presented to me,
and I recognized it.
Yet I wish not to put you to shame and have you exposed,
and that my gift may reach you without making it heavy upon you by making a display of benevolence,
but rather as one who is paying a debt."
And a certain poet came to him,
and began to recite poems before him.
And he replied:
"I do not understand what you are saying;
yes, I know that you want something."
And he ordered that five hundred gold dinars be given to him,
and a horse and garments for another five hundred.
And in the year 1480 of the Greeks,
Qilij Arslan, sultan of Iconium, took Caesarea of Cappadocia and Semandu from the Danishmendids.
And in the same year, which is the year 564,
564 of the Arabs,
Nur al-Din took the fortress of Ja'bar from Shihab al-Din, the Ma'addite emir from the Banu 'Uqayl,
giving him Saruj, al-Malahah, Bab Buzza'ah, and twenty thousand dinars.
